summary: Delivery remains strategically coherent and its codified top priorities still match the current product stack, but the strongest gaps are still proof-of-operation gaps: the Delivery-as-Code foundations are in place, yet the first real end-to-end pilot evidence pack, contract-grade gate logic, and operational scorecard/review loop are not yet visibly complete.

materialChanges.text: Delivery now has a canonical 08-research layer with domain map, radar, deep-dive index, doctrine, implications, and sources.
Delivery explicitly adopted an artifact-first research model with broad radar and bounded deep dives.
No material improvement yet in the top proof gap: one full inspectable Delivery v0.1 pilot evidence pack is still not visible in the reviewed product stack.

topPriorities.title: Run one real Delivery v0.1 pilot end to end and publish the evidence pack
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Delivery only becomes credible as a shipping system when one real or representative change has moved through activation, gate use, evidence capture, rollback discipline, and explicit pass/fail outcome.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. PRODUCT.md, PLAN.md, RISKS.md, the Delivery research implementation memo, and the assembly ACTIVATION/VERIFY docs all keep the first real pilot and canonical evidence pack as the highest-value next proof step.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Select one bounded Delivery v0.1 pilot in a consuming environment, run the full ACTIVATION and VERIFY path, and publish one inspectable evidence pack covering lane used, scope, gate applied, evidence captured, rollback notes, and verdict.

topPriorities.title: Upgrade the Delivery gate from checklist to contract
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Delivery reliability depends on gates being deterministic, risk-aware, and evidence-backed rather than dependent on operator interpretation.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. The strategy, governance posture, state-transition policy, risks, metrics, and VERIFY baseline all point to gate ambiguity as the next major control-quality weakness after basic scaffolding.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Convert the current checklist into a risk-classed contract with explicit required checks, evidence outputs, pass/fail logic, and at least one machine-checkable validation hook tied to the existing policy/governance path.

topPriorities.title: Make Delivery measurement and review operational, not aspirational
topPriorities.whyThisMattersNow: Delivery will not compound as a product unless weekly scorecards and reviews produce recurring evidence and concrete improvement decisions instead of remaining an intent surface.
topPriorities.currentStatus: Still current. METRICS.md and PLAN.md define the direction, but no clear product-local evidence in the reviewed stack shows the first low-noise weekly scorecard snapshot and review loop are already operating.
topPriorities.nextConcreteStep: Define the minimal weekly scorecard snapshot, run the first real review, and record one concrete improvement follow-through from the result.

constraints.title: No inspectable first real Delivery v0.1 pilot evidence pack is yet visible in the reviewed product stack
constraints.impact: Prevents Delivery from proving that its activation, verification, rollback, and evidence model works in a real consuming environment rather than only in design artifacts.

constraints.title: Delivery gate semantics are still stronger in policy/design intent than in contract-grade executable validation
constraints.impact: Leaves gate application vulnerable to interpretation drift and weakens comparability, enforcement, and confidence in release-readiness judgments.

risksOrOpportunities.title: Verification debt through thin activation/evidence practice
Security or authority regression under delivery pressure
Artifact-first research layer can make Delivery learning cumulative and easier to synthesize

researchDelta.summary: Delivery adopted a broad domain map and radar with three bounded deep-dive themes: end-to-end Delivery v0.1 proof, gate contract hardening, and delivery scorecard/review operationalization.

proposedTdeActions.title: Prioritize one real bounded Delivery v0.1 pilot with canonical evidence-pack output
proposedTdeActions.why: This is the clearest bottleneck between Delivery's documented design and credible operational proof.

proposedTdeActions.title: Define the next contract-grade gate increment with machine-checkable validation
proposedTdeActions.why: This closes the main control-quality gap between checklist guidance and policy-backed, reproducible release/readiness judgment.

proposedTdeActions.title: Use the new Delivery research layer to broaden surveillance while keeping only three active deep dives
proposedTdeActions.why: This tests whether artifact-first research improves signal quality without polluting Control Tower context.
